idea_taken: Forecasting, not just classifying: 30-day headache history (37.64% of model performance) beat prodrome (11.13%).
how_it_shaped_this_project: ML evaluation reports AUC-style honesty and a time/history lesson; the project design (REPORT.md §4.3) proposes a 4-8 week daily diary so a future forecasting model has the history it needs. No time-series is faked from the 400 cross-sectional records.

idea_taken: How you model time matters: time-series AUC 0.84 vs decision tree 0.59 and foundation model 0.55.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Model comparison in Part A is head-to-head on the same split/CV, like Faisal's comparison — and the survey template (Q15) collects the daily data a time-series model would need. Sensitivity/recall is reported per class (REPORT.md §7.2), so a good headline accuracy cannot hide missed cases.

idea_taken: Student survey design: validated screens (MS-Q, MIDAS, GAD-7, PHQ-9), multinational, n=5,954.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Survey template Q1-Q3, Q12 use validated-screen style items and a disability count; REPORT.md warns to report screened-positive, never diagnosed, and to stratify by sex/faculty instead of convenience-only sampling.

idea_taken: Care gap in students: 82% used analgesics, only 11.7% sought medical help; 52.1% screened positive in a 94.2%-female sample.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Survey template Q13-Q14 measure care-seeking and medicine use; REPORT.md uses Almomani for triggers/disability patterns, NOT for prevalence.

idea_taken: Missed diagnosis is patterned: men diagnosed before referral 57.0% vs women 73.8%; pressing pain raises misses in men.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Missed-diagnosis risk flags in Part C (below) and survey Q4-Q5, Q7 capture the atypical features (bilateral, pressing, no worsening with activity) that drive misses.

idea_taken: 43.3% misdiagnosed at first visit; first consult with a non-neurologist aOR 7.92; vertigo aOR 4.39.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Missed-diagnosis risk flags in Part C; survey Q13 records who was consulted first. Wide CIs (male aOR 95% CI 1.07-56.50) are quoted, not hidden.

idea_taken: Trigger awareness gap: stress recognised by 93.4%, but only 28.3% actively manage triggers and only 18% keep a diary.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Survey template Q8-Q11 measure trigger awareness AND action (diary, sleep schedule, stress techniques) — knowledge alone is not counted as management.

idea_taken: Real-world treatment evidence must show the denominator: >=50% responders 69%, but only for 74/215 (34%) who completed >=24 weeks.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Part B prints the completers denominator next to every responder rate; REPORT.md never quotes 69% without '74/215'.

idea_taken: Patient satisfaction matters, not only migraine days: TSQM 77.2, MMD -8.7, 65% >=50% responders — in completers only.
how_it_shaped_this_project: Part B compares Barbanti vs Cardona-Roca responder rates with their completers caveats side by side; survey Q14 asks about preventive use without recommending any drug.

idea_taken: Cautionary lesson: augmenting 400 records to 1,447 and claiming DNN 99.66% — no external validation, likely leakage.
how_it_shaped_this_project: NO augmentation anywhere in this project. Stratified split, 5-fold CV, per-class reporting, and this honesty note in the code, README and REPORT.
